title: Type system
lede: TypeScript's type surface reinterpreted for whole-program AOT compilation, so the divergences are about what a static native target can and can't model. Advanced type-level machinery — mapped/utility/conditional types, generics, intersections, typeof queries — is evaluated at compile time via monomorphization, then erased, and assertions (`as T`, `as const`, `satisfies`) and modifiers (`readonly`) are likewise erased rather than enforcing. The primitives are JS-faithful (`number` is an IEEE-754 double; `bigint` is arbitrary-precision), with the extended integer/float JSDoc types as the escape hatch for real fixed-width integer semantics.

entries.name: number → double
entries.description: A JS-faithful IEEE-754 double: 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004, 10 / 3 is 3.3333333333333335, 1 / 0 is Infinity. The explicit JSDoc integer types are the opt-in escape hatch when real integer semantics matter.
differences: A plain `number` past 2^53 loses precision exactly as JS does (`9007199254740993` is `…992`) — inherent to the double model, not a defect (use `int64`/`uint64` for exact 64-bit integers)
Mixing an explicit integer type with a bare literal promotes to double (`int32 / 2` is `3.5`); use two integer-typed operands for integer division

entries.name: string → ptr
entries.description: The string type, lowered to a pointer at the IR level.

entries.name: boolean → i1
entries.description: The boolean type, lowered to a single-bit i1.

entries.name: void
entries.description: The absence of a return value on a function.

entries.name: null / undefined
entries.description: The null and undefined values, represented as a sentinel null pointer.

entries.name: JSDoc extended integers
entries.description: A JSDoc @type override that gives a binding real fixed-width integer semantics: int8..int64 and uint8..uint64, with integer division, exact values past 2^53, and bit-width storage.

entries.name: JSDoc extended floats
entries.description: A JSDoc @type override selecting float32 or float64. Float-to-string is JS-faithful: the shortest decimal that round-trips, per ECMAScript Number::toString, so 1.1 + 2.2 prints 3.3000000000000003 and integer-valued floats drop the point. A float32 prints against its widened double.

entries.name: any
entries.description: A runtime-tagged value supporting declare/assign/reassign/print/typeof/=== plus bare any params and returns on every function shape. Objects and arrays box by reference — === is reference identity, typeof is "object".
entries.snippet:
let x: any = 5
x = "hello"
x = true
console.log(typeof x)   // boolean
differences: Arithmetic on an `any` is a clean compile error
Nested positions `any[]`/`{ x: any }` are clean compile errors
A boxed array keeps only its data pointer — length/elements aren't recoverable, so it stringifies to the `[object Array]` tag, not its contents

entries.name: unknown
entries.description: The type-safe counterpart to any, with the same Staged V1 scope: declare/assign/reassign/print/typeof/=== plus bare params and returns.
differences: Same as `any` (see above)

entries.name: never
entries.description: The bottom type. A (): never function that always throws works correctly.

entries.name: symbol
entries.description: V1 opaque unique values — Symbol()/Symbol("desc") (no new, Symbol is not a constructor), ===/!==, typeof, .description, .toString(). Uniqueness comes from the value's own heap-pointer identity, so two Symbol() calls with the same description are never equal.
differences: No dynamic property keys

No well-known symbols as runtime values (`Symbol.iterator`, etc.); the exceptions are `[Symbol.asyncIterator]` and `[Symbol.iterator]` recognized purely syntactically as class/object-literal computed-member keys, not evaluable `Symbol` values
No `Symbol.for`/`Symbol.keyFor` registry

entries.name: bigint
entries.description: Arbitrary-precision integers over a backend-agnostic ABI, selectable via -bigint=libtommath|gmp (default libtommath, public domain). Literals, the full arithmetic/bitwise operator set, same-type and cross-type-with-integer comparisons, typeof, ++/--, .toString([radix]), BigInt.asIntN/asUintN, Number(bigint), params/returns/fields/arrays, and BigInt(int|string) all work. Division/modulo by zero throws a catchable Error.
differences: No `.toLocaleString()` (an `Intl`-shaped gap)

entries.name: T | null (nullable)
entries.description: A single-branch T | null uses a presence-flagged nullable-scalar slot ({ i1, T }), so a genuine null is distinguishable from a legitimately-present 0 everywhere — ??, === null, printing, JSON — across locals, params, returns, fields, and Maps. A multi-branch A | B | null is handled by the union box instead.
entries.snippet:
let present: number | null = 0
let absent: number | null = null
console.log(present ?? 42)      // 0
console.log(absent ?? 42)      // 42

entries.name: Object types (interfaces / inline {})
entries.signature: interface Point { x: number; y: number }
entries.description: Interfaces, inline {} shapes, and type aliases. A literal's fields are coerced against the declared type wherever one is known — variable annotation, function parameter/return/default, array element type, or nested field — not just the literal's own self-inferred type.

entries.name: Array types T[]
entries.description: Homogeneous arrays, stored as a { ptr, i64 } aggregate.

entries.name: Promise<T>
entries.description: The Promise<T> type for async values.

entries.name: Function types (a: T) => R
entries.description: Function types, represented as a closure struct { funcPtr, envPtr }.

entries.name: Map<K,V>
entries.description: The Map<K,V> collection, with separate helpers per key/value combination (<string,number>, <string,string>, etc.).

entries.name: Set<T>
entries.description: The Set<T> collection.

entries.name: Union types beyond T | null
entries.description: The same runtime box as any/unknown with a checked member set on top, statically restricted to the declared members at every assignment/call/return boundary. A narrowed local unboxes to the concrete member; an object member to its typed pointer.
entries.snippet:
let x: string | number = "hello"
console.log(typeof x)    // string
x = 42
console.log(typeof x)    // number
differences: Scalar members (`number`/`string`/`boolean` + `null`/`undefined`), object/interface/class members (one object member, or ≥2 as a **discriminated union** sharing a first-position string-literal tag), and a `ReadableStream` member; array/`ArrayBuffer` members, number-literal tags, and a non-first-position tag aren't supported

Usable at the top level of a var declaration/function param/return and as an **object field** (checked + boxed at construction); as an **array element** it's still rejected (element-level checking not wired)

Flow narrowing is for a union **local** via `typeof`/truthiness/`==null` (if/else branches + early return); a field/element, discriminated-union tag, `switch (typeof x)`, and `as` casts aren't narrowed; an un-narrowed object union has no field access

entries.name: Intersection types
entries.description: An object-type intersection collapses at resolveType into one merged ObjectType — member fields concatenated, compatible duplicates deduped — with no runtime tag, unlike a union. & binds tighter than |. Works as a named interface, inline {}, or type alias member, and in variable/param/return/field/array-element positions.
differences: Object-type members only — a non-object member (scalar/function/array/tuple/union, all `never` in TS), or a generic-with-type-arguments member, is a clean compile error

A field declared with conflicting **non-object** types across members is rejected under `-compat=strict` (default); the `-compat=js` TS-faithful `never`-field is not yet implemented, so a conflict is currently rejected in both modes (same-named **object** fields are recursively intersected instead — `{ x: A } & { x: B }` ⇒ `x: A & B`)
Inherits object types' missing-field leniency: a partial object literal for an `A & B`-typed target is not rejected (a pre-existing object-literal behavior, not intersection-specific)

entries.name: Tuple types
entries.description: A fixed-arity, heterogeneous, positional value stored as a fixed-shape struct. Supports the tuple literal, constant-index read and assignment, .length (compile-time constant), destructuring (including nested and for-of), and array-shaped rendering. Map/Array/Object.entries() return real [K, V] tuples.
entries.snippet:
const point: [number, number] = [3, 4]
console.log(point[0])              // 3
const [name, value] = point
differences: No rest/optional/named elements
Constant index only — no non-constant index; compound assignment to an element (`t[0] += x`) is a clean rejection
No array methods (`.map`/`.filter`/…) on a tuple (`.length` works)
Not supported nested in `any` or a union

entries.name: Mapped & utility types
entries.signature: type Clone = { [K in keyof T]: T[K] }
entries.description: Partial/Required/Readonly/NonNullable/Pick/Omit/Record, the general mapped form { [K in keyof T]: V }, keyof, indexed access T[K], and string-literal types — all evaluated at compile time to concrete object types via the monomorphization seam, no runtime representation.
entries.snippet: type Clone = { [K in keyof User]: User[K] }
differences: `Partial`/`Required`/`Readonly` are structural no-ops — the object model already zero-fills omitted fields and does no mutation checking; the visibly-effective utilities are `Pick`/`Omit`/`Record`
Mapped value body handles `T[K]` (homomorphic), a bare `K`, a concrete type (uniform), or `T[K]` wrapped one level in `Array`/`Promise`/`Set`; a `T[K]` nested deeper isn't substituted
No key remapping (`as`) or modifier-removal (`-?`/`-readonly`); `?`/`readonly` are accepted but near-no-ops
String-literal types resolve to `string` — the literal value is not narrowed/enforced
An unrecognized `Name<Args>` (or a malformed `Pick`/`Omit`) is not yet a clean rejection

entries.name: Conditional types (T extends U ? X : Y)
entries.statusRow: Conditional types (T extends U ? X : Y)
entries.signature: type ElementOf<T> = T extends Array<infer E> ? E : T
entries.description: Evaluated at compile time off the monomorphized (concrete) check type — generic type aliases, infer capture, and a structural assignability predicate. Nested conditionals are right-associative.
entries.snippet:
type ElementOf<T> = T extends Array<infer E> ? E : T
const one: ElementOf<number[]> = 7
const raw: ElementOf<string> = "hi"
differences: `infer` supported for `Array<infer E>`/`Promise<infer V>` and a bare `infer R`; function-signature inference (`(...) => infer R`) and deeper `infer` nesting are deferred
`assignable` is structural width subtyping (objects), element-wise (arrays), IR-equality with numeric leniency (scalars) — not full variance

entries.name: Generics on user functions/interfaces/classes
entries.description: V1 (default) is monomorphization — one specialized implementation per distinct combination of concrete types actually used. Covers function identity<T>, interface Box<T>, class Box<T>, and multiple type parameters <K, V>. <T extends X> constraints are parsed and enforced (structural width subtyping). V2 /** @erased */ compiles a generic function's body once, with no name mangling.
differences: No explicit call-site type arguments for a *function* (`identity<number>(5)`) — inference-only, blocked by the `a<b>(c)` grammar ambiguity (a generic class still takes an explicit `new Box<T>(...)` list)
A generic function needs an inferable `T`/`T[]`-typed parameter for each of its type parameters
Map/Set/Promise/closure/dynamic type arguments are a clean rejection (scalars, arrays, and object/interface/class types are supported)
V2 `@erased` covers functions only (not interfaces/classes) and bare `T` positions only — `T[]` or `T` nested in an object field is a clean compile error
Arithmetic on an erased `T` hits the same "operator on any/unknown" rejection as plain `any`

entries.name: Index signatures ({ [k: string]: T })
entries.description: A string index signature types a dictionary of arbitrary string keys, backed by a map.
differences: String key only, map-backed — `d[key]` read/write, an object-literal initializer, and `Object.keys/values/entries` + `for…of` all work
A numeric index (`[i: number]: T`) and a mixed named+index shape (`{ id: number; [k: string]: T }`) are clean rejections
`JSON.stringify` of an index-signature dict is a clean rejection (no field table to walk) — build it from `Object.keys(...)`; a map-iterating stringify path is deferred

entries.name: typeof type queries (type T = typeof x)
entries.statusRow: typeof type queries (type T = typeof x)
entries.description: Derives a type from an existing value without restating its shape, usable as a type alias, an inline annotation, or a parameter/return type.
differences: Resolves the referenced value's type (a variable's object/scalar/array type, or a function's type), walking a `typeof a.b` member path — usable as a `type` alias, an inline annotation, or a parameter/return type. A function-local binding shadowing a top-level one of the same name isn't distinguished (the top-level wins), and an unresolvable query degrades to the `number` default rather than erroring

entries.name: Type assertions (x as T, as const, satisfies T)
entries.statusRow: Type assertions (x as T, as const, satisfies T)
entries.description: Parsed as a left-associative postfix on any expression; as const and satisfies T are likewise identity.
differences: **Erased, not enforcing** — the assertion is accepted and dropped: the value is unchanged and keeps its *own* inferred type, so `as T` does not re-type the expression (a sound cross-representation reinterpret isn't modeled). This matches TS's runtime erasure but not its static narrowing/widening; a cast the code *relies on* for typing won't take effect

entries.name: Template literal types ( a-${T} )
entries.description: Template literal types parse in a type position (no-substitution, multi-substitution, and []-suffixed forms) and resolve to `string` — the literal pattern isn't narrowed or enforced, the same simplification string-literal types use.
differences: Erased to `string` — the literal pattern is not narrowed/enforced.

entries.name: readonly T[] array-type modifier
entries.description: The readonly array-type modifier parses in variable/parameter/return/field positions.
differences: **Erased, not enforcing** — `readonly number[]` and `readonly [T, U]` parse (in variable/parameter/return/field positions), but the modifier is dropped and mutation is not prevented, the same stance as `Readonly<T>` and the mapped-type `readonly` modifier. The `ReadonlyArray<T>` alias form is not covered

entries.name: Ambient declarations (declare const/function/class/module/namespace)
entries.description: declare ambient declarations describe types the environment provides; carrying no implementation, they are parsed and erased.
differences: Parsed and erased — the no-body/no-init forms and the brace-bodied `global`/`module`/`namespace`/`class` blocks all compile away. Ambient declarations describe externally-provided values; under whole-program AOT they have no target to bind to, so a runtime *use* of a declared binding this compiler doesn't itself provide is an ordinary `undefined variable` error
